Agency and contracting activity U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Acquisition Solutions, Construction, Finance, Administrative and Interagency Agreements Division (CFAIAD), Construction, A/E Branch, Section 1 (Regions 1-4), Cincinnati, Ohio. 2. The nature and description of the actions being approved The purpose of this justification for other than full and open competition is to execute the extension of services clause pursuant to FAR 52.217-8 that was not evaluated as part of the original contract award. Contract 68HERD21D0001 is a single-award indefinite-delivery / indefinite-quantity (ID/IQ) hybrid contract (RFO FAR Subpart 16.5) for operations and maintenance of the EPA Research Triangle Park campus. Contract Number: 68HERD21D0001 Contractor: VGS Infrastructure Services, Inc. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency�s needs The Agency requires continuation of operations and maintenance support services (facility repair, replacement, and construction) on a twenty-four-hour, seven-day-a-week basis at RTP facilities provided both on the basic contract and under existing task orders that have schedules extending beyond the current completion date of the contract. This includes providing comprehensive management, training, licensed personnel with facility access, tools, and labor necessary to perform all functions, operations, and tasks. Specific critical areas of the PWS are the routine inspection and monitoring of the facility infrastructure, including electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems. Maintaining the building automation systems (BAS) controls. Emergency response preparedness, such as backup power, fire protection system maintenance, chemical spills, water damage/leaks, and inclement weather. Without ongoing support for these functions, the risks to personnel health, government property, and ongoing research would be unacceptable. Please refer to the attached contract performance work statement for a complete description of the support required under the contract. 4. Statutory authority 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) - the supplies or services are available from only one responsible source, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements, as implemented at RFO FAR 6.103-1 (the successor to FAR 6.302-1 under the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul, adopted at EPA by class deviation IPN 25-06 / RFO-2025-06). 5. A statement demonstrating the unique qualifications of the contractor or the nature of the actions requiring use of authority Due to the critical nature of the RTP facilities operation and maintenance support services provided via this contract, a lapse in services cannot occur. Any interruptions to the services required to maintain buildings on the campus that house active laboratories present unacceptable operational and safety risks to the Agency and employees who occupy these spaces. In accordance with FAR 52.217-8, because the six-month extension was not evaluated in the initial competition, the Government does not treat its exercise as pre-competed and instead justifies it here as available from only one responsible source. Only the current contractor, VGS Infrastructure Services, Inc., can provide uninterrupted continuation of the required services. VGS infrastructure Services, Inc, possesses the necessary site clearances, staffing, infrastructure, and institutional knowledge necessary to continue to support and execute the contract requirements for the short period of time authorized under FAR 52.217-8, until a follow-on contract is awarded. Securing these critical support services from an alternative source would require the execution of a competitive procurement process that cannot be awarded before the current contract period of performance expiration on September 30, 2026. No other source can complete the in-progress tasks/services under the current orders and any other source would be required to begin the work again. Furthermore, re-procuring the unfinished balance of non-severable services that are currently underway under existing task orders issued pursuant to the ID/IQ portion of the contract, is not feasible and would result in the termination of these tasks for the Government�s convenience, the need to reprocure unfinished construction projects with divided design responsibility, duplicated mobilization expense, and warranty fragmentation on installed equipment. Another contractor would need to obtain the necessary site-security clearances which would result in months of unacceptable delays on systems serving active laboratories. The costs incurred by the Government to reprocure this requirement before the current expiration date are not in the best interest of the Government and would likely exceed the price of the contemplated extension. The requested extension is for a six-month period, priced at the contract�s existing competed rates, which were previously negotiated and determined fair and reasonable. 6. A description of efforts to ensure that offers were solicited from as many potential sources as possible, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR Part 5 and, if not, which exception under Part 5 applies. A Notice of Intent for Sole Source Modification was posted on SAM.gov on August 27, 2026, and closed on September 11, 2026. No sources other than the current contractor were solicited due to the Government�s need to maintain uninterrupted continuation of the incumbent�s services. The underlying contract was placed under the competitive procedures applicable at award and FAR 52.217-8 was included in the solicitation for the contract. Therefore, potential offerors were on notice that EPA might exercise the option. 7. The extension costs are based on the contractor�s existing Option Period IV pricing for a total increase of (Redacted) for the six-month extension period. description: Notice of Intent to Award / Sole Source The Navajo Area Indian Health Service, Tsaile Health Center intends to award a non-competitive, sole sourced purchase order to ScriptPro USA, Inc., for Compact Robotic Prescription Dispensing System services. The anticipated period of performance is from January 01, 2026 to December 11, 2026 with three one-year option periods. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 339112- Surgical and Medical Instrument Manufacturing with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. The Proposed Contractor is the only organization uniquely qualified to provide the required services to ensure that there is no interruption in services that could impact direct patient care. The proposed contractor's equipment is currently on-site, fully installed, and is currently being used by Pharmacy staff to provide direct patient care testing services. The ScriptPro system is proficient with RPMS and manages the automated dispensing system workflow. Tsaile Pharmacy Department effectively checks in patient(s) while Pharmacy Techs operate ScriptPro's robotic medication dispensary to match doctor scripts with RPMS system. If the ScriptPro machine support services are down or unavailable, the pharmacy team is not able to support direct patient care services for medication dispensing. Changing out systems would negatively impact direct patient care. This notice of intent to award a sole source contract is not a request for competitive proposals. There will be no solicitation available for competitive quotes. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. If no affirmative written response is received by Closing Date/Time, the contract will be issued without further notice. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement base upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Any solicitation resulting from the analysis of information obtained will be announced to the public in Federal Business Opportunities. However, responses to this notice will not be considered adequate responses to a solicitation. No proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in your response. The Government reserves the right to use any non-proprietary technical information in any resultant solicitation(s).

title: CONTRACTS & CAPITAL FOR VETERANS RESOURCE FAIR
description: CONTRACTS & CAPITAL FOR VETERANS RESOURCE FAIR The U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command, MICC-Campbell, in partnership with the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Kentucky District Office and other federal, state, and local resource partners, will participate in the Contracts & Capital for Veterans Resource Fair at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. This event is designed to connect veteran small business owners and entrepreneurs with procurement and lending resources that can help support business growth and federal contracting opportunities. Attendees will have the opportunity to network with procurement and resource representatives and learn how to pursue federal contracts and access SBA-backed lending options for veteran-owned small businesses. Representatives from the following organizations are expected to participate: MICC-Campbell SBA Kentucky District Office SBA Tennessee District Office Directorate of Public Works Fort Campbell - AAFES Fort Campbell - MWR Employment Navigator and Partnership Program (ENAPP) Kentucky and Tennessee Small Business Development Centers Veterans Business Outreach Center U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Kentucky and Tennessee APEX Accelerators Fortera Credit Union Department of Veterans Affairs Date and Time: 18 November 2026 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. Central Standard Time Location: Army Community Service (ACS) 1501 William C. Lee Road Fort Campbell, KY 42223 Parking: Attendess may park in the ACS parking lot or in the over flow lot across from ACS building (Dolan Pool parking lot). See map in attachments. Installation Access: Personnel requiring a gate pass may obtain one in person at the Gate 7 Access Control Point or online at https://pass.aie.army.mil/. Attendees are encouraged to obtain their pass in advance to allow sufficient time for installation access. Who Should Attend: Veteran small business owners, veteran entrepreneurs, and businesses interested in learning more about federal contracting opportunities, procurement resources, and SBA-backed lending. Registration: No registration is required to attend this event. Attendees are encouraged to arrive early to allow sufficient time for installation access and event check-in. Notice: This event is for informational and networking purposes only. It is not a solicitation, request for quotation, request for proposal, or other contract opportunity. No contract award will result from this event. Questions: Questions regarding this event should be directed to: Ms. Aishia M. Jackson aishia.m.jackson.civ@army.mil (270) 798-7800 Please monitor this announcement for updates. Event details are subject to change.

Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition: Spacecraft Optical Navigation and Autonomy Modules (Contract 80ARC026C0006)
description: NASA Ames Research Center awarded Contract 80ARC026C0006 to EraDrive, Inc., 221 Forest Avenue, Palo Alto, California 94301 (Unique Entity ID PLUQPL2X6CN3), on September 22, 2026, on a sole-source basis. The contract is a firm-fixed-price definitive commercial contract for two (2) flight-qualified EraDrive Autonomy Modules, one optical hardware-in-the-loop stimulator, one electrical ground support equipment (EGSE) kit with integration, test, verification, and validation tooling, associated nonrecurring engineering, and engineering support services. The modules provide vision-based, Global Positioning System (GPS)-independent positioning, navigation, and timing; autonomous onboard maneuver planning; and autonomous optical detection, identification, and orbit determination of resident space objects. Award amount: $11,925,000. Total value including all options: $13,000,000. Period of performance: September 23, 2026 through December 31, 2028. This action was awarded using other than full and open competition under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The acquisition was conducted under the commercial procedures of FAR Part 12. A notice of NASA�s intent to award this sole-source contract was published to the Government Point of Entry, SAM.gov, on June 16, 2026 and closed July 1, 2026. One capability statement was received in response to that notice, from Rhea Space Activity, Inc. It was evaluated by the technical office and did not establish an alternative source capable of satisfying the requirement within the program schedule. NASA Ames Research Center is the servicing, awarding, and administering agency under an Economy Act reimbursable interagency agreement with the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, which is funding this effort under its Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies (APFIT) program. The approved Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition is attached. Portions have been redacted in accordance with FAR 6.301. This notice is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals, and no solicitation will be issued. No response is required. Correction posted October 20, 2026: This notice as originally published, and Section 10 of the attached Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition, contained a scrivener�s error stating that no capability statements were received in response to notice 80ARC026R0008. One capability statement was received, from Rhea Space Activity, Inc., on June 30, 2026, and was evaluated. It did not establish an alternative source capable of satisfying the requirement within the program schedule. The sole-source determination and the August 11, 2026 approval are unchanged. See the attached correction memorandum.

title: Netherlands – Endangered species protection services – Natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) en een gebiedsdekkend (Pré) Soortenmanagementplan (SMP)
description: Gemeente Beekdaelen beoogt met deze aanbestedingsprocedure een gebiedsdekkend soortenmanagementplan (SMP), een pré-SMP en de uitvoering van natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) te verwerven, inclusief begeleiding van de bijbehorende aanvragen omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag. Gemeente Beekdaelen beoogt met deze aanbestedingsprocedure een gebiedsdekkend soortenmanagementplan (SMP), een pré-SMP en de uitvoering van natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) te verwerven, inclusief begeleiding van de bijbehorende aanvragen omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag. De opdracht bestaat uit één overeenkomst voor de ontwikkeling van drie onderdelen. 1. Het uitvoeren van de opdracht Natuurvriendelijk isoleren voor gemeente Beekdaelen; 2. Het ontwikkelen van een Pré-Soortenmangementplan, inclusief het verzorgen en begeleiden van de bijbehorende aanvraagprocedure voor een (tijdelijke) omgevingsvergunning voor een flora- en faunactiviteit bij het bevoegd gezag en ondersteuning bij eventuele bezwaar- en beroepsprocedures voor Gemeente Beekdaelen; 3. Het ontwikkelen van een gebiedsdekkend SMP, inclusief het verzorgen en begeleiden van de bijbehorende aanvraagprocedure voor een gebiedsgerichte omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna-activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag en ondersteuning bij eventuele bezwaar- en beroepsprocedures voor de gemeente Beekdaelen. Beekdaelen telt ongeveer 35.903 inwoners met ongeveer 16.915 woningen. Hiervan zijn 72,8% koopwoningen. Gemeente Beekdaelen heeft een totale oppervlakte van 7.840 hectare en de gemiddelde dichtheid van de adressen is 508 adressen per km2. Het onderzoek richt zich op het bebouwde gebied. Dit bedraagt ongeveer 12.6 km². Het onderzoeksgebied dient als basis voor de prijsvorming. Het definitieve onderzoeksgebied zal in samenspraak met de Provincie Limburg moeten worden vastgesteld gedurende de eerste fase van de opdracht. Gemeente Beekdaelen wenst binnen drie jaar na opdrachtverstrekking het NVI te hebben voltooid en te beschikken over een goed werkend SMP, inclusief een gebiedsgerichte omgevingsvergunning.

title: Switzerland – Health and social work services – Mise en œuvre et gestion du Réseau Santé Genève
description: Nature et importance Le système de santé suisse connaît une augmentation continue de ses coûts, qui exerce une pression croissante sur les ménages et les finances publiques. À Genève, plus de 200'000 personnes ont bénéficié de subsides d’assurance-maladie en 2025, représentant 38 % de la population. Dans ce contexte, le Canton souhaite développer, au travers du projet Béluga, un modèle de santé plus durable, plus efficient et plus accessible, reposant sur l’articulation entre la Caisse Santé Genève et un réseau santé intégré, le Réseau Santé Genève. Le Réseau Santé Genève constitue l’un des deux piliers du projet. Il vise à améliorer la coordination et la continuité des soins, à renforcer la prévention et la prise en charge des maladies chroniques et à favoriser une utilisation plus efficiente des ressources du système de santé. Cette organisation doit contribuer à l’objectif de permettre aux assurés du modèle alternatif de bénéficier, à terme, d’une prime LAMal inférieure de 20 % à la prime moyenne cantonale. L’appel d’offre pour la Caisse Santé Genève est accessible sous le No Simap : 44094.

Les licences doivent être garanties durant toute la durée du contrat. title: Switzerland – Special-purpose motor vehicles – Beschaffung von Kanal TV-Inspektionsfahrzeug
description: Das Gewässerschutzgesetz verpflichtet die Betreiber öffentlicher Abwasseranlagen zur regelmässigen Zustandskontrolle des Kanalnetzes. Die ERZ Entwässerung der Stadt Zürich führt diese Inspektionen im gesamten Stadtgebiet durch und unter-sucht Kanäle mit Rohrdurchmessern von DN 80 bis DN 3000. Die Zustandsaufnahmen dienen der Werterhaltung der Infrastruktur, der Sicherstellung der Betriebssicherheit sowie dem Schutz von Gewässern und Umwelt. Für die Durchführung dieser Arbeiten werden spezialisierte Kanalinspektionsfahrzeuge mit moderner Kamera- und Inspektionstechnik benötigt. Die Anforderungen an Verfügbarkeit, Einsatzflexibilität sowie technische Leistungsfähigkeit sind aufgrund der unterschiedlichen Kanalgrössen und Einsatzbedingungen hoch. Gestützt auf die Klimaschutzziele der Stadt Zürich sowie die Fahrzeugpolitik der Stadt muss die Fahrzeugflotte bis spätestens 2035 mit wenigen unvermeidbaren Ausnahmen auf erneuerbare Antriebssysteme umgestellt werden. Im Rahmen dieser Zielsetzungen ist für die Ersatz- beziehungsweise Neubeschaffung zwingend ein vollelektrisch betriebenes Fahrzeug vorzusehen. Mit der Beschaffung soll sichergestellt werden, dass die gesetzlichen Inspektionsaufgaben weiterhin zuverlässig, wirtschaftlich und umweltgerecht erfüllt werden können. Gleichzeitig leistet das Fahrzeug einen Beitrag zur Reduktion von CO 2 Emissionen, Lärmemissionen und Umweltbelastungspunkten (UBP) im Sinne der städtischen Netto-Null-Strategie. Das zu liefernde neue Trägerfahrzeug muss zwingend ein Elektrofahrzeug sein und soll ein maximales Gesamtgewicht von 7.5t aufweisen und mit einem Auf- / Ausbau ausgestattet werden. Der Auf- /Ausbau des Trägerfahrzeugs beinhaltet zudem einen Bedienraum für eine Person (Einstieg seitlich, in Fahrtrichtung rechts) sowie einen Heckraum, in welchem die TV Anlage, sowie die dazu benötigten Geräte und Werkzeuge untergebracht sind. title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – FE 05.0217/2026/FGB - „Alternative Bindemittel zur Bodenbehandlung im Erdbau des Straßenbaus“
description: Die normierten Bindemittel Kalk und Zement werden wirksam zur Bodenbehandlung eingesetzt. Der Nachteil jedoch ist, dass Kalke und Zemente eine hohe CO2-Emission verursachen. Es soll daher erkundet werden, welche alternativen Bindemittel zur nachhaltigen Bodenbehandlung verwendet werden können. Bei dem genormten Bindemittel Zement besteht die Bestrebung, durch klinkerreduzierte Zemente eine bessere CO2-Bilanz zu erreichen. Die Reduktion der Klinkerphasen bedeutet aber auch eine Reduktion der festigkeitsbildenden Komponenten. Insofern wäre durch Eignungsprüfungen zu untersuchen, ob die klinkerreduzierten Zemente für die Bodenbehandlung verwendbar sind. Die Zugabe von Asche (z.B. Papierasche, Flugasche) bewirkt im Boden eine Veränderung der Verdichtungseigenschaft als auch eine Festigkeitsbildung. Bei Aschen stellen sich neben den Fragen nach der Wirkungsweise aber außerdem Fragen nach der gleichbleibenden und verlässlichen Zusammensetzung (Schwankungsbreite der Zusammensetzung) sowie nach den umweltrelevanten Inhaltstoffen. Es gibt Sonderbindemittel auf dem Markt, die als Bindemittel oder als Additive verwendet werden. Bodenbehandlungsadditive dienen der Verbesserung der Materialeigenschaften des Ausgangsmaterials und der Reduktion der anschließend zuzugebenden Bindemittelmenge. Das Ziel der Forschungsarbeit ist es, die Wirkungsweise ausgewählter alternativer Bindemittel zu untersuchen und mit der Wirkungsweise genormter Bindemittel zu vergleichen. Des Weiteren soll eine Grundsatzprüfung für alternative Bindemittel sowie eine Eignungsprüfung für Bodenbehandlungen mit nicht genormten Bindemitteln erarbeitet werden. Es liegt im Inte-resse des Bundes, einen nachhaltigen Straßenbau zu betreiben, was sowohl bedeutet, dass Bindemittel verwendet werden, die den Boden wirksam verbessern oder dauerhaft verfestigen als auch umweltverträglich, emissionsarm, ressourcenschonend und ökonomisch sind.

title: Norway – Repair and maintenance services of building installations – Painting and covering services
description: Background Tønsberg municipality needs to establish a new framework agreement for painting and covering services as the existing contract has expired and must be replaced. The procurement shall ensure that the municipality still has access to the necessary services for ongoing maintenance and planned upgrades in the municipality's buildings and sites. The municipality has a continual and increasing need for external and internal surface treatment in, among other things, schools, nurseries, health buildings and other purpose-built buildings. The objective of the procurement is to ensure the right quality, predictable delivery and effective follow-up of assignments across entities. The framework agreement shall contribute to good use of resources, clear call-off routines and stable delivery ability throughout the entire contract period. The aim is to have a parallel model with two tenderers, where assignments are generally offered to the tenderer ranked as number one and thereafter the tenderer ranked second if the first tenderer is unable to deliver within the set deadlines. The estimated total value is approx. NOK 35,000,000 excluding VAT over four years. Description of the assignment The procurement is for a framework agreement for the delivery of painting and covering services for Tønsberg municipality. The delivery shall cover the municipality ́s need for work connected to paint, floor coverings and other surface treatment, both indoor and outdoor. The framework agreement shall cover ongoing maintenance, minor repairs and planned redecorating works in municipal buildings and sites. The assignments can vary in size and complexity and will i.a. apply to work in schools, nurseries, health buildings and other buildings in daily use. Emphasis will be put on call-offs under the framework agreement being made efficient and predictable, with a quick response, good coordination with the municipality ́s units and equal quality in the deliveries, regardless of which tenderer carries out the assignment. The delivery shall also support the need for good documentation, including status reports and assignment related documentation. The work shall be able to be carried out in a way that ensures safe operation and limits disadvantages for users of the buildings. This is particularly important in buildings with vulnerable user groups and high activity, such as schools, nurseries and health buildings.

title: Norway – Pest-control services – Pest control and control - Framework agreement
description: Background Tønsberg municipality has a continual need for services and materials connected to control, prevention and control of pests in the municipality ́s buildings and associated facilities. The existing agreement expires and the municipality needs to establish a new framework agreement that ensures continued safe, efficient and predictable follow-up in the agreement period. The aim of the procurement is to cover the municipality ́s need for both planned and emergency services within pest control, at the same time that the municipality receives a combined and transparent agreement for the area. The framework agreement shall contribute to early pest detection, reduce the risk of consequential damage, strengthen health, environment and safety and facilitate equal practice and quality across the municipality ́s buildings and sites. The municipality emphasises a long-term cooperation with a tenderer who can offer professional advice, good documentation and close follow-up of the assignments. It is also important that the delivery supports the municipality ́s goal of efficient use of resources, good contract follow-up, as well as climate and environmental considerations in the implementation of the services. Description of the assignment The procurement is for a framework agreement with one tenderer for the delivery of services and accompanying material for the control and control of pests. The contract shall include both preventive work, periodic inspections and acute call-outs as needed. The delivery shall cover the municipality ́s need for municipal buildings as well as relevant outside areas and technical infrastructure, including, among other things, roads, water and sewage. The assignment includes pest control both indoor and outdoor, including pest management in kitchen areas and other vulnerable locations. The service shall mainly cover inspections, assessment of scope and reason, implementation of the necessary measures, use and delivery of necessary material such as traps and baiting stations, as well as written reporting for each assignment. The tenderer shall also be able to make recommendations on preventive measures and contribute to a better overview, traceability and history per building or facility. The assignment can include pest control, including rats, mice, wall animals, cockroaches, silverfish and beards, ants, moths and other relevant insects. The extent in the contract period can vary, and the stated volume is only an estimate based on previous consumption. The delivery shall therefore be scaleable and adapted to the municipality ́s actual need throughout the contract period.
